sanskrit: dūrapātī maheṣvāsaḥ kṛtāstro yuddhadurmadaḥ dṛḍhāstraś citrayodhī ca dhārtarāṣṭro mahābalaḥ
english: A great archer whose shafts fly far, accomplished in arms, drunk with the lust of battle, firm in his weapons and a wily fighter — such is the mighty son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: atyantasukhasaṃvṛddho mānitaś ca mahārathaiḥ kṛtī ca satataṃ pārtha nityaṃ dveṣṭi ca pāṇḍavān
english: Reared amid boundless ease and honored by the great car-warriors, ever adept, O Pārtha, he forever hates the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tena yuddham ahaṃ manye prāptakālaṃ tavānagha atra vo dyūtam āyātaṃ vijayāyetarāya vā
english: With him, O sinless one, I judge that the hour of battle has come for you; here the dicing of you both has arrived again — for victory, or else for the other end.

sanskrit: atra krodhaviṣaṃ pārtha vimuñca cirasaṃbhṛtam eṣa mūlam anarthānāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathaḥ
english: Here, O Pārtha, loose the venom of your wrath, long stored up; this great car-warrior is the very root of the Pāṇḍavas' miseries.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ prāptas tavākṣepaṃ paśya sāphalyam ātmanaḥ kathaṃ hi rājā rājyārthī tvayā gaccheta saṃyugam
english: He has come within your reach — behold the fruit of your own striving. How else should a king bent on the kingdom come to do battle with you?

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tv idānīṃ saṃprāpta eṣa te bāṇagocaram sa yathā jīvitaṃ jahyāt tathā kuru dhanaṃjaya
english: By good fortune he has now come within the range of your arrows; act so, O Dhanaṃjaya, that he may yield up his life.

sanskrit: aiśvaryamadasaṃmūḍho naiṣa duḥkham upeyivān na ca te saṃyuge vīryaṃ jānāti puruṣarṣabha
english: Deluded by the intoxication of sovereignty, he has never known sorrow, nor does he know your valor in battle, O bull among men.

sanskrit: tvāṃ hi lokās trayaḥ pārtha sasurāsuramānuṣāḥ notsahante raṇe jetuṃ kim utaikaḥ suyodhanaḥ
english: For the three worlds, O Pārtha, with their gods, demons, and men, cannot prevail to conquer you in battle — how much less Suyodhana alone?

sanskrit: sa diṣṭyā samanuprāptas tava pārtha rathāntikam jahy enaṃ vai mahābāho yathā vṛtraṃ puraṃdaraḥ
english: By good fortune he has come near your chariot, O Pārtha; slay him, mighty-armed one, as Puraṃdara slew Vṛtra.

sanskrit: eṣa hy anarthe satataṃ parākrāntas tavānagha nikṛtyā dharmarājaṃ ca dyūte vañcitavān ayam
english: For he has ever striven for your ruin, O sinless one, and by trickery he cheated the King of Righteousness at the dice.

sanskrit: bahūni sunṛśaṃsāni kṛtāny etena mānada yuṣmāsu pāpamatinā apāpeṣv eva nityadā
english: Many a cruel deed has this man of evil mind wrought, O giver of honor, against you who are blameless, and that without ceasing.

sanskrit: tam anāryaṃ sadā kṣudraṃ puruṣaṃ kāmacāriṇam āryāṃ yuddhe matiṃ kṛtvā jahi pārthāvicārayan
english: That ignoble, ever-base man, who follows only his own willful desire — bend your mind to noble battle, O Pārtha, and slay him without hesitation.

sanskrit: nikṛtyā rājyaharaṇaṃ vanavāsaṃ ca pāṇḍava parikleśaṃ ca kṛṣṇāyā hṛdi kṛtvā parākrama
english: Holding in your heart, O son of Pāṇḍu, the theft of the kingdom by fraud, the dwelling in the forest, and the abuse of Kṛṣṇā, put forth your might.

sanskrit: diṣṭyaiṣa tava bāṇānāṃ gocare parivartate pratighātāya kāryasya diṣṭyā ca yatate 'grataḥ
english: By good fortune he moves within the range of your arrows; by good fortune he strives at the forefront to thwart your purpose.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā jānāti saṃgrāme yoddhavyaṃ hi tvayā saha diṣṭyā ca saphalāḥ pārtha sarve kāmā hi kāmitāḥ
english: By good fortune he knows at last that he must fight with you in battle; by good fortune, O Pārtha, all your cherished desires are now fulfilled.

sanskrit: tasmāj jahi raṇe pārtha dhārtarāṣṭraṃ kulādhamam yathendreṇa hataḥ pūrvaṃ jambho devāsure mṛdhe
english: Therefore slay in battle, O Pārtha, this son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the disgrace of his line, as of old Jambha was slain by Indra in the war of gods and demons.

sanskrit: asmin hate tvayā sainyam anāthaṃ bhidyatām idam vairasyāsyās tv avabhṛtho mūlaṃ chindhi durātmanām
english: With him slain by you, let this host, left without a lord, break apart; this is the final bath that ends the feud — cut away the root of these evil-souled men.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca taṃ tathety abravīt pārthaḥ kṛtyarūpam idaṃ mama sarvam anyad anādṛtya gaccha yatra suyodhanaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: "So be it," answered Pārtha; "this is the very deed for me. Heeding nothing else, drive on to where Suyodhana stands.

sanskrit: yenaitad dīrghakālaṃ no bhuktaṃ rājyam akaṇṭakam apy asya yudhi vikramya chindyāṃ mūrdhānam āhave
english: By whom our kingdom was so long enjoyed unopposed — let me press forward in the fray and strike off his head in battle.

sanskrit: api tasyā anarhāyāḥ parikleśasya mādhava kṛṣṇāyāḥ śaknuyāṃ gantuṃ padaṃ keśapradharṣaṇe
english: Would that I might reach, O Mādhava, the day of reckoning for the undeserved torment of Kṛṣṇā, for the seizing of her hair.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ vādinau hṛṣṭau kṛṣṇau śvetān hayottamān preṣayām āsatuḥ saṃkhye prepsantau taṃ narādhipam
english: Speaking thus, the two Kṛṣṇas, exultant, urged on their splendid white steeds in the battle, eager to come at that lord of men.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samīpaṃ saṃprāpya putras te bharatarṣabha na cakāra bhayaṃ prāpte bhaye mahati māriṣa
english: When your son had come near the two, O bull of the Bharatas, he showed no fear, though a great peril had come upon him, O venerable one.

sanskrit: tad asya kṣatriyās tatra sarva evābhyapūjayan yad arjunahṛṣīkeśau pratyudyāto 'vicārayan
english: For this all the warriors there honored him: that he went out without hesitation to meet Arjuna and Hṛṣīkeśa.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvasya sainyasya tāvakasya viśāṃ pate mahān nādo hy abhūt tatra dṛṣṭvā rājānam āhave
english: Then from all your host, O lord of peoples, there rose a great roar there, beholding the king in the battle.

sanskrit: tasmiñ janasamunnāde pravṛtte bhairave sati kadarthīkṛtya te putraḥ pratyamitram avārayat
english: While that dreadful clamor of men went up, your son, making light of the danger, held back his foe.

sanskrit: āvāritas tu kaunteyas tava putreṇa dhanvinā saṃrambham agamad bhūyaḥ sa ca tasmin paraṃtapaḥ
english: But the son of Kuntī, checked by your bowman son, flew into still greater fury; and that scorcher of foes flamed up against him.

sanskrit: tau dṛṣṭvā pratisaṃrabdhau duryodhanadhanaṃjayau abhyavaikṣanta rājāno bhīmarūpāḥ samantataḥ
english: Seeing the two, Duryodhana and Dhanaṃjaya, thus enraged against each other, the kings of terrible aspect gazed upon them from every side.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu pārthaṃ saṃrabdhaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca māriṣa prahasann iva putras te yoddhukāmaḥ samāhvayat
english: But beholding Pārtha enraged, and Vāsudeva too, O venerable one, your son, as though smiling, eager for the fight, called them out.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭo dāśārhaḥ pāṇḍavaś ca dhanaṃjayaḥ vyākrośetāṃ mahānādaṃ dadhmatuś cāmbujottamau
english: Then the joyful Dāśārha and the son of Pāṇḍu, Dhanaṃjaya, raised a great war-cry and blew their finest conch-shells.

sanskrit: tau hṛṣṭarūpau saṃprekṣya kauraveyāś ca sarvaśaḥ nirāśāḥ samapadyanta putrasya tava jīvite
english: Seeing the two so full of gladness, the Kauravas on every side grew hopeless of your son's life.

sanskrit: śokam īyuḥ paraṃ caiva kuravaḥ sarva eva te amanyanta ca putraṃ te vaiśvānaramukhe hutam
english: And the Kurus all fell into deepest grief, and deemed your son already cast as an oblation into the mouth of Vaiśvānara.

sanskrit: tathā tu dṛṣṭvā yodhās te prahṛṣṭau kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau hato rājā hato rājety ūcur evaṃ bhayārditāḥ
english: Beholding thus the joyful Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava, those warriors, stricken with fear, cried out, "The king is slain, the king is slain!"

sanskrit: janasya saṃninādaṃ tu śrutvā duryodhano 'bravīt vyetu vo bhīr ahaṃ kṛṣṇau preṣayiṣyāmi mṛtyave
english: But Duryodhana, hearing the clamor of the host, said: "Let your fear depart; I shall send the two Kṛṣṇas to death."

sanskrit: ity uktvā sainikān sarvāñ jayāpekṣī narādhipaḥ pārtham ābhāṣya saṃrambhād idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having so spoken to all his soldiers, that lord of men, looking for victory, addressed Pārtha and in his fury uttered these words:

sanskrit: pārtha yac chikṣitaṃ te 'straṃ divyaṃ mānuṣam eva ca tad darśaya mayi kṣipraṃ yadi jāto 'si pāṇḍunā
english: "O Pārtha, whatever weapon you have learned, divine or human, show it on me at once — if indeed you were begotten of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: yad balaṃ tava vīryaṃ ca keśavasya tathaiva ca tat kuruṣva mayi kṣipraṃ paśyāmas tava pauruṣam
english: Whatever strength and valor are yours, and Keśava's as well, exert it on me at once — let us see your manhood.

sanskrit: asmat parokṣaṃ karmāṇi pravadanti kṛtāni te svāmisatkārayuktāni yāni tānīha darśaya
english: Out of our sight, men tell of deeds you are said to have done, deeds meant to win your master's favor — show those very deeds here."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktvārjunaṃ rājā tribhir marmātigaiḥ śaraiḥ pratyavidhyan mahāvegaiś caturbhiś caturo hayān
english: Saṃjaya said: Having so spoken to Arjuna, the king pierced him in return with three arrows that pierced the vitals, and with four swift shafts struck his four horses.

sanskrit: vāsudevaṃ ca daśabhiḥ pratyavidhyat stanāntare pratodaṃ cāsya bhallena chittvā bhūmāv apātayat
english: And he pierced Vāsudeva with ten arrows between the breasts, and cutting his goad with a broad-headed shaft, cast it to the ground.

sanskrit: taṃ caturdaśabhiḥ pārthaś citrapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ avidhyat tūrṇam avyagras te 'syābhraśyanta varmaṇaḥ
english: Him Pārtha, unflurried, swiftly pierced with fourteen stone-whetted shafts of gaily feathered shanks; but they glanced off from his armor.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vaiphalyam ālokya punar nava ca pañca ca prāhiṇon niśitān bāṇāṃs te cābhraśyanta varmaṇaḥ
english: Seeing them fall fruitless, he loosed again fourteen more sharp arrows; and these too glanced off from his armor.

sanskrit: aṣṭāviṃśat tu tān bāṇān astān viprekṣya niṣphalān abravīt paravīraghnaḥ kṛṣṇo 'rjunam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Seeing those twenty-eight shafts that he had shot fall in vain, Kṛṣṇa, slayer of hostile heroes, spoke these words to Arjuna:

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ paśyāmi śilānām iva sarpaṇam tvayā saṃpreṣitāḥ pārtha nārthaṃ kurvanti patriṇaḥ
english: "A thing never seen before I now behold — your arrows creep away like stones. The feathered shafts you send, O Pārtha, accomplish nothing.

sanskrit: kaccid gāṇḍīvataḥ prāṇās tathaiva bharatarṣabha muṣṭiś ca te yathāpūrvaṃ bhujayoś ca balaṃ tava
english: Is the life of the Gāṇḍīva still the same, O bull of the Bharatas? Is your grip as of old, and the strength of your two arms?

sanskrit: na ced vidher ayaṃ kālaḥ prāptaḥ syād adya paścimaḥ tava caivāsya śatroś ca tan mamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ
english: If this be not the last hour decreed by fate, come today for you and for this foe — then tell me, who ask you.

sanskrit: vismayo me mahān pārtha tava dṛṣṭvā śarān imān vyarthān nipatataḥ saṃkhye duryodhanarathaṃ prati
english: Great is my wonder, O Pārtha, to see these arrows of yours fall vainly in battle against Duryodhana's chariot.

sanskrit: vajrāśanisamā ghorāḥ parakāyāvabhedinaḥ śarāḥ kurvanti te nārthaṃ pārtha kādya viḍambanā
english: Your arrows, terrible as the thunderbolt and the lightning, cleavers of an enemy's body, accomplish nothing — what mockery is this today, O Pārtha?"

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca droṇenaiṣā matiḥ kṛṣṇa dhārtarāṣṭre niveśitā ante vihitam astrāṇām etat kavacadhāraṇam
english: Arjuna said: This device, O Kṛṣṇa, was set by Droṇa upon the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; this fitting of armor is the last of the lore of weapons.

sanskrit: asminn antarhitaṃ kṛṣṇa trailokyam api varmaṇi eko droṇo hi vedaitad ahaṃ tasmāc ca sattamāt
english: In this armor, O Kṛṣṇa, even the three worlds lie hidden and warded; Droṇa alone knows this art, and I from that best of men.

sanskrit: na śakyam etat kavacaṃ bāṇair bhettuṃ kathaṃ cana api vajreṇa govinda svayaṃ maghavatā yudhi
english: This armor cannot be pierced by arrows in any wise, O Govinda — no, not by the thunderbolt itself in the hand of Maghavat in battle.

sanskrit: jānaṃs tvam api vai kṛṣṇa māṃ vimohayase katham yadvṛttaṃ triṣu lokeṣu yac ca keśava vartate
english: Knowing all this, O Kṛṣṇa, why do you seek to bewilder me? Whatever has passed in the three worlds, and whatever now comes to pass, O Keśava,

sanskrit: tathā bhaviṣyad yac caiva tat sarvaṃ viditaṃ tava na tv evaṃ veda vai kaś cid yathā tvaṃ madhusūdana
english: and whatever shall be — all of it is known to you; nor does any other know it as you do, O slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: eṣa duryodhanaḥ kṛṣṇa droṇena vihitām imām tiṣṭhaty abhītavat saṃkhye bibhrat kavacadhāraṇām
english: This Duryodhana, O Kṛṣṇa, wearing this armor wrought by Droṇa, stands fearless in the battle.

sanskrit: yat tv atra vihitaṃ kāryaṃ naiṣa tad vetti mādhava strīvad eṣa bibharty etāṃ yuktāṃ kavacadhāraṇām
english: But the rite that must here accompany it he does not know, O Mādhava; like a woman he wears this well-fitted armor in vain.

sanskrit: paśya bāhvoś ca me vīryaṃ dhanuṣaś ca janārdana parājayiṣye kauravyaṃ kavacenāpi rakṣitam
english: Behold the might of my arms and of my bow, O Janārdana; I shall overcome the Kaurava, guarded by his armor though he be.

sanskrit: idam aṅgirase prādād deveśo varma bhāsvaram punar dadau surapatir mahyaṃ varma sasaṃgraham
english: This shining armor the Lord of the gods once gave to Aṅgiras; and again the lord of the gods gave to me that armor together with its mystic rite.

sanskrit: daivaṃ yady asya varmaitad brahmaṇā vā svayaṃ kṛtam naitad gopsyati durbuddhim adya bāṇahataṃ mayā
english: Though this armor of his be divine, or fashioned by Brahmā himself, it shall not save that fool today, smitten by my arrows.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktvārjuno bāṇān abhimantrya vyakarṣayat vikṛṣyamāṇāṃs tenaivaṃ dhanurmadhyagatāñ śarān tān asyāstreṇa ciccheda drauṇiḥ sarvāstraghātinā
english: Saṃjaya said: Having so spoken, Arjuna, charging his arrows with sacred spells, drew them back; but as he drew those shafts set at the middle of the bow, the son of Droṇa cut them apart with his weapon that destroys all weapons.

sanskrit: tān nikṛttān iṣūn dṛṣṭvā dūrato brahmavādinā nyavedayat keśavāya vismitaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ
english: Seeing those arrows cut down from afar by that knower of the sacred word, the white-steeded warrior, amazed, made it known to Keśava:

sanskrit: naitad astraṃ mayā śakyaṃ dviḥ prayoktuṃ janārdana astraṃ mām eva hanyād dhi paśya tv adya balaṃ mama
english: "This weapon I cannot loose a second time, O Janārdana, for the weapon would then turn and slay me; yet behold today my strength."

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ kṛṣṇau navabhir nataparvabhiḥ avidhyata raṇe rājañ śarair āśīviṣopamaiḥ bhūya evābhyavarṣac ca samare kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau
english: Then Duryodhana, O king, pierced the two Kṛṣṇas in battle with nine smooth-jointed arrows like venomous serpents, and again rained his shafts upon Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava in the fray.

sanskrit: śaravarṣeṇa mahatā tato 'hṛṣyanta tāvakāḥ cakrur vāditraninadān siṃhanādaravāṃs tathā
english: At that great rain of arrows your men rejoiced, and raised the din of instruments and roars like lions.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho raṇe pārthaḥ sṛkkaṇī parisaṃlihan nāpaśyata tato 'syāṅgaṃ yan na syād varmarakṣitam
english: Then Pārtha, enraged in battle, licking the corners of his mouth, looked but could find no limb of his that was not guarded by the armor.

sanskrit: tato 'sya niśitair bāṇaiḥ sumuktair antakopamaiḥ hayāṃś cakāra nirdehān ubhau ca pārṣṇisārathī
english: Then with sharp arrows, well loosed and like Death himself, he made his horses lifeless, and both his flank-charioteers as well.

sanskrit: dhanur asyācchinac citraṃ hastāvāpaṃ ca vīryavān rathaṃ ca śakalīkartuṃ savyasācī pracakrame
english: The valiant one cut his gaily-wrought bow and his hand-guard, and the Ambidextrous Archer set about to splinter his chariot to pieces.

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ ca bāṇābhyāṃ tīkṣṇābhyāṃ virathīkṛtam avidhyad dhastatalayor ubhayor arjunas tadā
english: And Duryodhana, now bereft of his chariot, Arjuna then pierced in both palms of his hands with two keen arrows.

sanskrit: taṃ kṛcchrām āpadaṃ prāptaṃ dṛṣṭvā paramadhanvinaḥ samāpetuḥ parīpsanto dhanaṃjayaśarārditam
english: Seeing him fallen into so dire a strait, tormented by Dhanaṃjaya's shafts, the foremost bowmen rushed up, eager to rescue him.

sanskrit: te rathair bahusāhasraiḥ kalpitaiḥ kuñjarair hayaiḥ padātyoghaiś ca saṃrabdhaiḥ parivavrur dhanaṃjayam
english: With chariots by the many thousands, with elephants and horses arrayed, and with raging floods of foot-soldiers, they hemmed in Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: atha nārjunagovindau ratho vāpi vyadṛśyata astravarṣeṇa mahatā janaughaiś cāpi saṃvṛtau
english: Then neither Arjuna nor Govinda, nor even their chariot, could be seen, so enveloped were they by the great rain of weapons and the throngs of men.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno 'stravīryeṇa nijaghne tāṃ varūthinīm tatra vyaṅgīkṛtāḥ petuḥ śataśo 'tha rathadvipāḥ
english: Then Arjuna, by the might of his weapons, smote that host; there, maimed by the hundred, fell the chariots and the elephants.

sanskrit: te hatā hanyamānāś ca nyagṛhṇaṃs taṃ rathottamam sa rathastambhitas tasthau krośamātraṃ samantataḥ
english: Slain and being slain, they yet hemmed in that noblest of chariots; halted in its course, it stood there, ringed about for a krośa on every side.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaṃ vṛṣṇivīras tvarito vākyam abravīt dhanur visphārayātyartham ahaṃ dhmāsyāmi cāmbujam
english: Then the hero of the Vṛṣṇis swiftly said to Arjuna: "Twang your bow with all your might, and I shall blow my conch."

sanskrit: tato visphārya balavad gāṇḍīvaṃ jaghnivān ripūn mahatā śaravarṣeṇa talaśabdena cārjunaḥ
english: Then, twanging the Gāṇḍīva mightily, Arjuna smote his foes with a great rain of arrows and with the clap of his bowstring on his palm.

sanskrit: pāñcajanyaṃ ca balavad dadhmau tāreṇa keśavaḥ rajasā dhvastapakṣmāntaḥ prasvinnavadano bhṛśam
english: And Keśava blew the Pāñcajanya loud and shrill, the edges of his eyelashes clogged with dust, his face streaming heavily with sweat.

sanskrit: tasya śaṅkhasya nādena dhanuṣo nisvanena ca niḥsattvāś ca sasattvāś ca kṣitau petus tadā janāḥ
english: At the blast of that conch and the twang of that bow, the men, both the spiritless and the stout-hearted, fell then to the earth.

sanskrit: tair vimukto ratho reje vāyvīrita ivāmbudaḥ jayadrathasya goptāras tataḥ kṣubdhāḥ sahānugāḥ
english: Freed of them, the chariot shone like a cloud driven on by the wind; thereupon the guardians of Jayadratha, with their followers, were thrown into turmoil.

sanskrit: te dṛṣṭvā sahasā pārthaṃ goptāraḥ saindhavasya tu cakrur nādān bahuvidhān kampayanto vasuṃdharām
english: But the guardians of the lord of the Sindhus, seeing Pārtha suddenly upon them, raised cries of many kinds, making the earth tremble.

sanskrit: bāṇaśabdaravāṃś cogrān vimiśrāñ śaṅkhanisvanaiḥ prāduścakrur mahātmānaḥ siṃhanādaravān api
english: Those great-souled warriors sent forth fierce twangings of arrows mingled with the blare of conches, and roars like lions as well.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā ninadaṃ ghoraṃ tāvakānāṃ samutthitam pradadhmatus tadā śaṅkhau vāsudevadhanaṃjayau
english: Hearing that terrible din arisen from your men, Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya then blew their conches.

sanskrit: tena śabdena mahatā pūriteyaṃ vasuṃdharā saśailā sārṇavadvīpā sapātālā viśāṃ pate
english: By that mighty blast this earth was filled, with its mountains, its sea-girt isles, and its nether realms, O lord of peoples.
